questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Many pilgrims died in a stampede while boarding (1)/ a private ferry to the holy place on (2)/ the ﬁrst day of the ten day long festival. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The entire sentence is grammatically correct.
 
• **Part (1): “while boarding a private ferry”**
 
 
• “While boarding” is a correct present participial phrase showing the time/ongoing action.
 
• It correctly modifies “Many pilgrims”, the subject of the sentence.
 
• The verb–object structure boarding a private ferry is grammatically sound.
 
 
 
• **Part (2): “on the first day of the ten day long festival”**
 
 
• The preposition “on” is correctly used with specific days.
 
• “First day” is a countable, definite time reference, so “the” is appropriate.
 
• “Ten day long” functions as a compound adjective describing “festival” and is acceptable in exam usage.
 
 
 
• **Overall sentence correctness:**
 
 
• Subject–verb agreement is correct (pilgrims died).
 
• Tense is consistent (simple past for a completed event).
 
• All modifiers are logically and grammatically placed.
 
 

Hence, the entire sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Companies in countries as the United States (1)/ left out of the trade pacts could face (2)/ disadvantages when trying to tap fast growing Asian markets. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration. We often get confused between like & S. **Like **is used as preposition before noun to should relativeness. Whereas, **as **is used to describe function of a person or thing. Here, **the United States **is a proper noun and it is not performing any action. So, preposition **like **should be used instead of **as. **Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **Companies in countries like the United States left out of the trade pacts could face disadvantages when trying to tap fast growing Asian markets.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word.Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Why ______ your friend set this meeting?
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Here, concept of simple past tense is brought under consideration. Since, there is a rule in grammar English. Whenever a question is being asked in past tense, tense helping verb **did **is used with verb’s first form, I.e. true verb. Since, main verb **set **is used here in its true form. So, use **did **in the blank to make it grammatically correct. Hence, option 1 i.e. **did **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **Why did your friend set this meeting?

Clearly, the word **tempo **best expresses the meaning of the given word 'rhythm'. Hence, option 2 i.e. **tempo **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

The quality of service (providing) was excellent especially in the hospitals run by charitable trusts and religious foundations.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Since, the verb used here is **was **which is used in past tense. Hence, options 1 & 2 are eliminated. If we use **providing, **it will be used as a gerund (Verb+ing). Gerunds are form of verbs that are used as noun. But, the noun is already mentioned at the beginning. Hence, option 4 is also eliminated. Thus, option 3 i.e. **provided **is the correct answer.

Note :- **Provided **is used as an intransitive verb. Intransitive verb does not take a direct object. 

**Correct sentence - **The quality of service provided was excellent especially in the hospitals run by charitable trusts and religious foundations.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

People in the remote village of Kerela are now totally self sufﬁcient and liberal and no longer (waited) till people from urban areas dish out empowerment as a special privilege or favor.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Since, the main verb **are **which is used in the sentence is a present form. Hence, same tense should be followed through out the whole sentence i.e. simple present tense. Thus, options 2 & 4 are eliminated. Also, **people **is a plural noun. So, according to sub-verb agreement, verb should also be plural. Thus, option 3 is eliminated.Hence, replace **waited **with **wait. **Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **People in the remote village of Kerela are now totally self sufﬁcient and liberal and no longer wait till people from urban areas dish out empowerment as a special privilege or favor.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

Real happiness

P: in material 

Q: possessions alone

R: does not lie
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

The starter of the sentence ends with an abstract noun **happiness**, so it cannot be followed by a noun directly i.e. **possessions. **Hence, option 4 is eliminated. Now, among rest of the combinations, we can only apply logic. It says that real happiness is not measured only by things you own. Hence, option 3 i.e. **RPQ **is the correct answer.

**Correct sequence - **Real happiness does not lie in material possessions alone.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

He drove his

P: slimy road to

Q: reach Shimla 

R: car through
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Clearly, a sentence does not end with a preposition. Hence, options 1 & 2 are eliminated. A preposition is used before a noun but not a verb. Thus, the sequence RQ i.e. **through reach **is grammatically incorrect. Hence, option 4 is also eliminated. Thus, option 3 i.e. **RPQ **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **He drove his car through slimy road to reach Shimla.

questions.question: equipment has given ______ to various
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

On looking at the above mentioned passage, we observe that it is based how use of technology has given birth to various types of pollution in our environment. Industrial waste, uses of technological devices, etc. had contributed in increasing pollution. 

The starter of the passage explains that it is because of uses of technological equipment that we use which has led various types of pollution. Word **rise **which means 'to get up; to become active' is an appropriate answer for the blank. Hence, option 1 i.e. **rise **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **The use of technological equipment has given rise to various types of pollution.

questions.question: waste is ______ in the seas
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 2**

First of all, let's find out the meaning of given options :-

Crown - A headgear worn by a king and queen.

Thrown - To put in hurry; to cause to fall to the ground.

Drawn - To cause to move in a particular direction; to bring, take or pull out.

Moron - A stupid or foolish guy.

With reference to the context, word 'crown & moron' are not appropriate answers. Hence, options 1 & 4 are eliminated. Also, waste is not taken in a particular direction. Hence, option 3 is eliminated. So, option 2 i.e. **thrown **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **waste is thrown in the seas.

questions.question: the smoke ______ by factories
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Firstly, there is no word like **transmilted**, hence, option 4 is clearly eliminated.

Let's find out the meaning of other given options :-

Remitted - To transfer or send (money, a check, etc.) to a person or place, usually in payment.

Admitted - Confessed; taken in approval of something.

Emitted - To produce heat, light, gas or a smell by means of physical or chemical process.

With reference to the context, the smoke which is produced by the factories and vehicle causes air pollution, etc.

Hence, word **emitted **is an appropriate answer. Thus, option 3 i.e. **emitted **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **the smoke emitted by factories and vehicles causes air pollution, noise pollution is also a result of the production/ use of technological devices.

questions.question: waste has also ______ to soil
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 4**

First of all, helping verb used in the sentence is **has **which shows that the sentence is a perfect tense. Hence, verb's 3rd form should be followed here. Thus, the only appropriate word which best fits the blank is **led. **It means to bring forward, to increase. Hence, option 4 i.e. **led **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - ** Industrial waste has also led to soil pollution.

questions.question: Technological ______ has also given way to thermal
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

First of all,there is no word like 'repairment'. Hence, option 1 is clearly eliminated.

Now, let's find out the meaning of other given options :-

Increment - Something added or gained; addiction.

Advancement - Act of moving forward; progress.

Regression - The act of going back to a previous place.

With reference to the context, progress in technology has made a way for thermal, radioactive and light pollution.So, option 4 i.e. **advancement **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **Technological advancement has also given way to thermal, radioactive and light pollution.
